claim: Pw registers in an effect only when enabled; keyboardHandler false rejects, true consumes; otherwise contextHandler precedes fallback callback. An empty second argument does not prove a no-op command.
Qji closeOtherTabs uses an empty fallback nMi but a contextHandler selects bottom/right panel and calls closeOtherTabs on its active tab; origin-panel and isActive conditions remain significant.
Wyc previousTab/nextTab use empty fallback callbacks but keyboard/context handlers call Hyc with direction and originPanel, guarded by c8n.
rbc nextRecentThread/previousRecentThread have keyboardHandler effects and empty fallbacks; registration alone does not establish equivalent behavior for context-only invocation.

Ht and Ut each register git.commit/createPullRequest/createDraftPullRequest/createBranch. Ht commit may invoke Xe when r is present while Ut sets the commit state; enabled expressions also differ. One descriptor cannot collapse their contexts.
Dml approval commands delegate supplied onApprove/onDecline and enabled conditions; these generic registrations do not identify the MCP computer-use approval feature.
The native N metadata producer reads bound Pt and At, tests Ft access, and obtains filtered keymap data; a native metadata-to-menu association does not prove the effective renderer handler.
zG resolves the merged registry by IG.get(id); QG derives Electron menu-title metadata and HG tests requiredAccess. These are descriptor/access contracts, not business handlers.
Seven saved Pw/import calls use dynamic command IDs from parameters or records. The 80 literal IDs do not exhaust registration identities or prove unmatched declarations unused.
